title: AI and Lean settle Erdős problem 728 on factorial divisibility

passages: Are there infinitely many integers $a,b,n$ with $a\geq \epsilon n$ and $b\geq \epsilon n$ such that\[a! b! \mid n!(a+b-n)!\]and $a+b>n+C\log n$? #728: [EGRS75,p.91] number theory | factorials A question of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75].
Erdős [Er68c] proved that if $a!b!\mid n!$ then $a+b\leq n+O(\log n)$.

items.title_found: Resolution of Erd\H{o}s Problem #728: a writeup of Aristotle's Lean proof
items.meta_description: Abstract page for arXiv paper 2601.07421: Resolution of Erdős Problem #728: a writeup of Aristotle's Lean proof
passages: The system in question is a combination of GPT-5.2 Pro by OpenAI and Aristotle by Harmonic, operated by Kevin Barreto.

We provide a writeup of a resolution of Erdős Problem #728; this is the first Erdős problem (a problem proposed by Paul Erdős which has been collected in the Erdős Problems website) regarded as fully resolved autonomously by an AI system.
The overall strategy is similar to results regarding divisors of $\binom{2n}{n}$ studied earlier by Erdős and by Pomerance.
These "carry-rich but spike-free" choices of $m$ force the needed $p$-adic inequalities and the divisibility.
